sprint.goal: Build a lightweight Kanban project management app: REST API + minimal web UI. Users can create tasks, move them between Todo, In Progress, and Done, edit task details, and delete tasks.

tasks.title: Inspect the repository and define the Kanban architecture, API contract, data model, and integration plan.
Implement validated REST endpoints for creating, listing, reading, updating/moving, and deleting tasks using project conventions.
Implement the minimal three-column Kanban UI with create, move, edit, and delete interactions.
Review and implement the task persistence schema, migrations, constraints, and seed strategy required by the agreed API.
Create and run API and UI acceptance tests covering all task lifecycle actions and invalid inputs.
Review API and UI for input validation, unsafe rendering, error leakage, and authorization assumptions; report or remediate issues.
Create `schema.sql` only: SQLite `tasks` table with id, title, description, status, created_at, updated_at; enforce statuses todo, in_progress, done and add status ordering index.
Implement `app.py` and `requirements.txt` only: initialize SQLite from `schema.sql` and expose the agreed JSON task REST API with validation, correct 404 handling, and no frontend-file edits.
Implement `static/index.html`, `static/app.js`, and `static/styles.css` only: a minimal three-column board consuming the agreed REST API, with create, edit, move, and delete flows.

messages.content: Assigned architecture discovery and technical plan.
Assigned REST API implementation and validation.
Assigned minimal Kanban UI implementation.
Queued persistence schema and migration review for assignment when a slot opens.
Queued lifecycle and validation testing for assignment when implementation is ready.
Queued application security review for assignment when implementation is ready.

No application code exists yet. Please sequence database before backend and treat db-2/be-2/fe-2 as the implementation tasks; the earlier broad tasks overlap them and should be retired or redirected to avoid duplicate work.

Own only schema.sql. Contract: tasks(id INTEGER PK, title TEXT required 1-200 chars, description TEXT default '', status TEXT required default 'todo' constrained to todo|in_progress|done, created_at, updated_at); include an index on status.

API contract: GET /api/tasks; POST /api/tasks with {title,description?}, returns 201; GET /api/tasks/:id; PATCH /api/tasks/:id with any of title, description, status; DELETE /api/tasks/:id returns 204. JSON errors use {error: string}; invalid payload/status is 400 and missing IDs are 404. Use schema.sql, and own only app.py and requirements.txt.

Use GET /api/tasks on load; POST for creation; PATCH for edits and status moves; DELETE then remove/reload. Status keys are todo, in_progress, done. Own only static/index.html, static/app.js, static/styles.css; render user text safely with textContent, never innerHTML.
Backend task be-1 is blocked on database-owned schema.sql; please complete db-2 before scheduling backend implementation.
Please notify backend when schema.sql is ready; backend will initialize and use it without modifying it.

schema.sql is ready and validated with SQLite. It creates the tasks table, status/trimmed-title constraints, timestamps, a status/updated_at index, and an update timestamp trigger; you may proceed with API implementation.
Database persistence work is complete in schema.sql; backend is unblocked.
schema.sql is complete and validated; resume be-1 now using the architect's API contract. Keep ownership to app.py and requirements.txt.
Backend implementation is now unblocked. Remain queued until its API is complete, then implement the board against the documented contract.
Prepare lifecycle and invalid-input acceptance coverage after backend and frontend implementation are complete.
Prepare a final review focused on API validation and safe UI text rendering after backend and frontend implementation are complete.
db-2 duplicated completed db-1 work; schema.sql already meets the stated contract and requires no further changes.
Both database task records are complete and schema.sql is available. Please proceed with API implementation and report the endpoint verification results.
Backend remains the active dependency. Begin UI work as soon as backend reports the API ready.

Backend API is implemented in app.py and is ready for frontend integration. Python syntax and schema loading checks passed; runtime smoke tests could not run because Flask is unavailable locally and package installation cannot reach PyPI.

API is ready: GET/POST /api/tasks; GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/tasks/:id. POST accepts title and optional description; PATCH accepts title, description, and/or status (todo|in_progress|done). Success responses return task JSON; validation errors return {error} with 400, missing tasks return 404, and DELETE returns 204.
Please verify task create/list/read/update/status-move/delete flows plus 400 JSON validation and 404 behavior once Flask dependencies are installed.
Backend validates accepted fields and uses parameterized SQLite values; please review error handling and deployment configuration during the final pass.
Backend API is complete. Please report completion when the board integration is finished so QA can begin acceptance testing.
Prepare the API/UI acceptance pass, but report the missing Flask dependency and unavailable package network as a blocker if it prevents runtime execution. Capture static checks that remain possible.
Begin the final static security review now: verify API validation/parameterization and frontend safe rendering. Report any runtime checks blocked by the unavailable Flask dependency.
No API change is requested. Remain available to address QA or security findings after their review.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use a lightweight task model with Todo, In Progress, and Done states.
Sequence database design before final API integration, then UI, QA, and security validation.
Use Python Flask with the standard sqlite3 module because the repository has no existing application scaffold and this stack is minimal to run locally.
Use SQLite database file `kanban.db`, initialized from database-owned `schema.sql`; no ORM or authentication is required for this lightweight single-user scope.
Expose JSON endpoints at `/api/tasks`: GET collection, POST collection, GET item, PATCH item (including status transitions), and DELETE item.
Use lowercase API status values `todo`, `in_progress`, and `done`; map them to the UI labels Todo, In Progress, and Done.
Serve a dependency-free vanilla JavaScript UI from `static/`; keep HTML, JavaScript, and CSS exclusively frontend-owned, API files exclusively backend-owned, and schema exclusively database-owned.
Tasks are ordered in each column by most recently updated first unless a future explicit ordering field is added.
Use a portable idempotent SQLite schema (`IF NOT EXISTS`) instead of a separate migration framework for this initial lightweight application.
Enforce normalized state values and nonblank 1-200 character titles at the database boundary; update `updated_at` via trigger.
Database schema is complete and owned by the database role; backend may now consume it without editing it.
Retire the architect's overlapping db-2/be-2/fe-2 tracking tasks in favor of the already-assigned db-1/be-1/fe-1 work, using the architect's file boundaries and contract.
The duplicated db-2 record is complete with no additional database work; schema.sql remains the sole database-owned file.
Do not create further duplicate implementation tasks; use messages and existing task records to coordinate the remaining work.
Proceed with static QA/security review while treating runtime validation as an environment blocker, not an implementation completion signal.
